note: Published because a list of what a node will not do saves other nodes more work than a list of what it offers. If a future Starcom document appears to relax one of these, that document is the bug.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not gate anything on a credential
refusals.because: A claim describes; it never permits. Gating converts a statement into a permission and manufactures a central authority. Ratified network-wide as standard 5.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not publish salience alongside weight
refusals.because: Weight measures how much to trust a claim, never how much to care about it. The two were conflated once and it hid the largest finding in a set of 10,514.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not accept or relay intake rules about who a service admits
refusals.because: They are not publicly knowable. Supplying them would be guessing with an extra hop of laundering, and would poison the one dataset in the network that cannot be reconstructed.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not re-link opaque source tokens across rotation periods
refusals.because: A stable pseudonym plus locations is a movement pattern. The rotation is the protection, and correlating across it would defeat a boundary another node accepted a cost to provide.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not operate a payment, token, or market layer
refusals.because: EA-LEDGER exists and works. A second payments stack in the sense-making node duplicates a proven capability and sits badly beside claims that must be free to check.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not operate a trust or scoring API
refusals.because: Confidence is computed by the consumer from disclosed method. A central scorer is self-asserted trust wearing a different hat. Scorers stay plural.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not publish a claim naming a private individual
refusals.because: Address lines naming a person rather than a place are withheld, deliberately over-excluding. This rule exists because it was once broken.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not ask a receiving node to trust its redactor
refusals.because: A redactor that honestly documents its own incompleteness cannot also be the enforcement point. Receiving nodes should filter again on arrival, and neither side should read that as distrust.

refusals.rule: Starcom will not publish a claim whose weak backing it has not stated
refusals.because: A publisher that computes its own weakness and withholds it is worse than one that never computed it: the information existed and the consumer was denied it. Starcom shipped exactly that defect.
